es: Argumentar por escrito (como en una intervención de un minuto) con una postura clara, una concesión y cautela, y usar frases para ganar tiempo y cerrar.

teaching.en: I firmly believe that cities should have more trees.
teaching.es: Creo firmemente que las ciudades deberían tener más árboles.
teaching.explanationEs: Firmly refuerza la postura: abre la intervención con una opinión clara.
teaching.audioText: I firmly believe that cities should have more trees.

teaching.en: It's true that trees cost money, but they also save money later.
teaching.es: Es cierto que los árboles cuestan dinero, pero también ahorran dinero después.
teaching.explanationEs: It's true that… but… concede un punto del otro antes de defender el tuyo.
segments: It's true that trees cost money,
but they also save money later.
teaching.audioText: It's true that trees cost money, but they also save money later.

teaching.en: To some extent, the heat is a bigger problem than the cost.
teaching.es: Hasta cierto punto, el calor es un problema mayor que el costo.
teaching.explanationEs: To some extent matiza: no dices que sea totalmente así.
segments: To some extent, the heat is
a bigger problem than the cost.
teaching.audioText: To some extent, the heat is a bigger problem than the cost.

teaching.en: What I mean is that shade makes the city cooler.
teaching.es: Lo que quiero decir es que la sombra hace la ciudad más fresca.
teaching.explanationEs: What I mean is… sirve para aclarar o ganar un segundo para pensar sin perder el hilo.
teaching.audioText: What I mean is that shade makes the city cooler.

teaching.en: On the other hand, trees can block the view of shops.
teaching.es: Por otro lado, los árboles pueden tapar la vista de las tiendas.
teaching.explanationEs: On the other hand introduce el otro lado; block es tapar o bloquear.
segments: On the other hand, trees can
teaching.audioText: On the other hand, trees can block the view of shops.

teaching.en: So, in short, I would say the benefits outweigh the costs.
teaching.es: Así que, en resumen, yo diría que los beneficios superan a los costos.
teaching.explanationEs: In short cierra la intervención; outweigh: algo pesa más que otra cosa.
segments: So, in short, I would say
teaching.audioText: So, in short, I would say the benefits outweigh the costs.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención de un minuto: postura, concesión y cautela.

answer.text: I firmly believe that our city should close its centre streets to cars on Sundays. First, a car-free centre would be safer, especially for children and older people. It would also be quieter, so families could walk, talk and enjoy the shops. It is true that some drivers may find it inconvenient, and some shops could lose a few customers. To some extent, I understand that worry. However, it seems that more people would come on foot, and they would spend time and money in the centre. On the other hand, we could keep one street open for deliveries and for people who cannot walk far. In short, a car-free Sunday would make our centre safer, calmer and friendlier, and I believe the benefits outweigh the costs.
accepted: I firmly believe that our city should close its centre streets to cars on Sundays. First, a car-free centre would be safer, especially for children and older people. It would also be quieter, so families could walk, talk and enjoy the shops. It is true that some drivers may find it inconvenient, and some shops could lose a few customers. To some extent, I understand that worry. However, it seems that more people would come on foot, and they would spend time and money in the centre. On the other hand, we could keep one street open for deliveries and for people who cannot walk far. In short, a car-free Sunday would make our centre safer, calmer and friendlier, and I believe the benefits outweigh the costs.

My position is clear: the streets of the centre should be closed to traffic on Sundays. Admittedly, it may be difficult for people who live far away, and I agree that the plan needs good buses. Perhaps the city could add a free bus on those days. Even so, I am convinced that the change would help. Children could play, people could meet, and the air would probably be cleaner. Some say shops would suffer, but it seems that busy streets usually bring more customers. To sum up, a quiet Sunday centre would be a great gift to everyone, and I think it is worth a try.

feedback.es: Una buena intervención abre con una postura firme, concede un punto contrario, matiza con cautela y cierra con un resumen.

origin.text: Tema: ¿deberían cerrarse al tráfico las calles del centro los domingos? Escribe entre 100 y 140 palabras (lo que dirías en un minuto): expresa tu postura con claridad, concede un punto contrario, usa al menos una expresión de cautela (to some extent, may, perhaps, it seems) y cierra con In short o To sum up.
